- **LinkedIn post:** Tuesday is here, and so is this week's read. We compared three ways teams collect feedback on creative work: comments on the file, one consolidated note and a live review. Each one catches different problems, and using the wrong one at the wrong stage is how projects end up polishing a concept nobody agreed on. Read it here:
- **Primary reader:** Creative directors, design leads and account or project managers who run review rounds with clients or internal stakeholders.
- **Creative discipline:** Creative practice: feedback, review and approval (applies across design, video, web and presentation work).
- **Platform or company, if relevant:** None. The article is tool-agnostic.
- **Central development or question:** Which feedback method suits which stage of a creative project, and what does each method systematically miss?
- **Why readers will care:** Review rounds are where creative projects lose time and direction. The comparison gives leads a simple way to diagnose why rounds multiply.
- **Most interesting supported detail:** Pinned comments are spatial, but structural problems have no location. The format therefore discourages the most important feedback and turns the designer into an unauthorised referee. This is analytical observation, not a statistic.
- **Central argument:** Feedback methods do different jobs. Teams should choose by project stage (live for direction, consolidated note for priorities, pinned comments for polish) rather than defaulting to comments on the file.
- **Concrete takeaway:** State the type of feedback wanted in every review request and match the channel to it. Audit a past project by tagging pinned comments as detail or structure. Structural comments in late rounds indicate a missing direction review.
- **Article format:** The focused comparison (three ways of working), delivered in this week's comparison shape with a table.
- **Difference from the previous published article:** The previous article was a quick take on video editing workflows (the transcript as primary file). This one is a comparison of feedback practices, a different discipline, format and central question.

This article is about choosing feedback channels by project stage across all creative work. It does not cover brand compliance or embedding standards in tools.

How AI comment summarisation changes approval accountability, if specific features can be verified. Feedback on video specifically (timecoded comments versus cut reviews). How agencies price review rounds.
- **History summary:** Comparison of three feedback methods for creative work: pinned comments on the file, a single consolidated feedback note and live review sessions. The argument is that pinned comments suit polish but suppress structural feedback and pass conflicting opinions to the designer to referee. Consolidated notes force someone with authority to set priorities, and live reviews suit direction but need a same-day written summary.
